newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia to sell large stake in natgas distributor.
newsitem.headline: Colombia to sell large stake in natgas distributor.

text.p: The Colombian government said Friday it would sell its entire 60.6 percent stake in Gas Natural ESP, the country's largest distributor of natural gas to domestic consumers.

The company is currently run by state-owned oil company Ecopetrol in conjunction with Bogota power company Empresa de Energia de Bogota, which has a 20 percent holding, and a handful of smaller associates.
Natural gas distribution to residential consumers is still in infancy in Colombia, but is being heavily promoted by the Mines and Energy Ministry.
Most of the 444,000 cubic feet per day of natural gas Colombia extracts is used in thermo-electric power generation.
Ecopetrol will sell its 9.08 million shares in Gas Natural ESP on the country's three stock exchanges at a fixed price of 6,667 pesos per share.
The stock offering officially begins Saturday, though Colombia's exchanges will be closed. The sale will actually start on the next business day, Monday.

In its intial phase, until February 28, the offering will only be open to Gas Natural ESP workers, retirees, former employees and employee associations. After that, shares will offered to the general public.

Gas Natural ESP currently serves 300,000 homes in Bogota and Soacha, a town just southwest of the capital. An additional 700,000 homes are expected to be connected to the supply network by the year 2000.
